[PAPER_0049, relevance_score=0.295] If time-on-task moderates the Sans Forgetica effect, we expect an attenuated effect on memory when time is constrained to be equal between Arial and Sans Forgetica. However, when encoding is self-paced, we expected better memory for Sans Forgetica compared to Arial. Corroborating this, Kühl et al. (2014) showed that self-paced study produced better learning outcomes compared to constrained study time.

Because of this, we hypothesized that we would observe a disfluency effect for Sans Forgetica only when study time was self-paced.

items.deviation_information:
The paper applies a log transformation to study times, which was not found in the provided registration excerpts [PAPER_0071] [PAPER_0073] [PREREG_0006] [PREREG_0007]. Whether missing data were marked incorrect cannot be verified in the provided paper excerpts [PREREG_0007]. The paper refers to supplemental materials and analysis scripts, which are not part of the input [PAPER_0051].
